title: Protocol assurance ladder
question: What was checked, and what bounded readiness do those checks support?
principle: Assurance records structure, testing, review, and bounded readiness within a declared context. It is not a universal safety finding and says nothing about whether the protocol improves anyone's work. A protocol can reach the top of this ladder and still make its users slower — that is the other ladder's job to detect. One badge must never stand for both. Every rung means only what its check actually established: an offline check of the shipped examples is not the same as a live run of the protocol, and the rung names say so.

states.label: Draft
states.meaning: The procedure exists but has not passed its own checks.

states.label: Structure validated
states.meaning: Schema- and structure-valid: required fields present, enums and patterns satisfied, kernel steps mapped, and the file inventory matches the manifest. This is a check of the DOCUMENT, not of the protocol's behaviour or its semantic fidelity to the kernel.
states.established_by: tools/validate.js passes against protocol.schema.json and the structural kernel checks; MANIFEST.json matches the files on disk.

states.label: Example conformance validated
states.meaning: The worked examples SHIPPED IN THE PACK satisfy the acceptance tests under deterministic graders, and deliberately-bad fixtures are rejected by those graders (discrimination). This proves the acceptance tests are mechanised and discriminating against the pack's own examples. It does NOT run a model over a fresh task, observe real actions, or establish that a model executing the protocol would conform.
states.established_by: tools/eval-harness.js --tests passes, including discrimination cases, and evals designs are valid.
states.gate: example fixtures + graders (offline, no model execution)

states.label: Task set passed (minimum acceptance gates)
states.meaning: A live runner executed the protocol over the registered task set on a named model, and the FRESH outputs — RECOMPUTED by the verifier from the committed raw outputs, not trusted from a self-reported field — passed the pack's ACCEPTANCE GATES (completion, plus no detected deterministic compliance/external-action signal in the recorded output). This is a MINIMUM bar: it means the recorded outputs addressed the task and contained no detected prohibited-action signal. It does NOT authenticate the run, observe external systems, or mean the outputs were high quality or accurate — that is the productivity-evidence ladder's concern, and a protocol can hold this rung while showing NO_CLEAR_GAIN or a measured quality regression. The offline harness cannot grant it. NOTE: the deterministic acceptance is reproducible from the committed outputs; the model and blind-judge identities recorded in the result are self-reported and not authenticated (see KNOWN-LIMITATIONS).
states.established_by: A recorded live run whose committed raw outputs recompute a passing agent-with-protocol arm under the deterministic graders, bound by SHA-256 to the task set and the outputs file and to the protocol id + version.
states.gate: live run; acceptance recomputed from committed outputs

states.label: Cross-model reproduced
states.meaning: At least two separate live runs using distinct named models meet the minimum acceptance gates on the same registered task set and yield the same measured productivity-evidence outcome. This is cross-model consistency by the same evaluation system, not independent reproduction, model authentication or proof of benefit.
states.established_by: At least two separately recorded, hash-bound live runs on the same task set, using at least two distinct named models, with recomputed passing acceptance and the same implied evidence status.
states.gate: separate live runs; same task set and evidence outcome; >= 2 named models

states.label: Security reviewed
states.meaning: Permissions, external calls, and hostile-input behaviour have been inspected by a human, the static scan is clean, and any runtime enforcement path (sandbox, capability mediation) has been considered. The static scanner alone does not grant this.
states.established_by: tools/hostile-tests.js passes AND a human security review of scripts, adapters, and declared permissions is recorded.

states.label: Field ready
states.meaning: Suitable for a bounded real-world trial by intended users outside the development team. Requires a live-run history (>= TASKSET_PASSED), human security review, copy-and-run edition, formative usability evidence with representative intended users, and no open critical defect. It does not mean the protocol is beneficial. Blocked while productivity evidence is HARM_OR_REGRESSION_FOUND.
states.established_by: All lower gates plus a copy-and-run edition, operating instructions, live-run history, recorded formative usability with intended users, and no open critical failure.
states.gate: all + live runs + security review + accessibility artefacts + formative usability

states.label: Deprecated
states.meaning: No longer recommended. Kept for the record, withdrawn from active use.
states.established_by: A maintainer decision, a security withdrawal, or a retest trigger that the protocol no longer survives.
